topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
consensus_response: Frequency planning can effectively address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems by allocating separate frequency bands for each system, coordinating through beamforming or adaptive antennas to reduce interferences in shared frequency bands. The array factor of combined antenna patterns causes constructive and destructive interference, leading to severe interferences in shared frequency bands like S-band (2.65-2.69 GHz) and Ka-band (27.5-31.0 GHz). By separating frequency allocation or coordinating through beamforming/adaptive antennas, the trade-off between system capacity, performance, and interference levels can be optimized.
